summary: Crash when changing render distance java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 28084 out of bounds for length 26136
description: When changing render view distance via the option menu while standing inside a world, minecraft sometimes crashes with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. This can be best reproduced by spam-clicking the slider in random positions, although for me it crashed after only one click, the first time.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Singleplayer world with default settings.
3. Open Options -> Video Settings.
4. Change the Render Distance slider to a random position and click to apply.
5. Immediately change the Render Distance slider to another random position and click to apply again.
6. Repeat step 5 multiple times in quick succession (spam-clicking the slider).
7. Observe that the game crashes with a `java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.
Observed Behavior: When changing the render view distance in the options menu while inside a world, Minecraft occasionally crashes with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, specifically indicating that index 28084 is out of bounds for the length of 26136. This issue can be consistently reproduced by rapidly clicking the render distance slider in various positions, although in some instances, the crash occurs after only a single click. It is important to note that the crash does not appear to be dependent on the specific render distance setting, as it has been observed at different distances. The problem manifests itself in a way that disrupts gameplay, making it critical for developers to address this bug to enhance the overall stability of the game.
Expected Behavior: When changing the render view distance via the options menu while in a world, Minecraft should adjust the render distance smoothly without crashing. The game should dynamically update the view distance based on the slider's position, allowing users to select any desired distance without encountering an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. This functionality should work consistently across different gameplay scenarios and not lead to unexpected crashes.
